response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats, COUNT(DISTINCT f.player_id) AS cnt FROM fielding f JOIN player p ON p.player_id = f.player_id GROUP BY p.bats), s AS (SELECT bats, cnt, SUM(cnt) OVER () AS total, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT bats, cnt AS player_count, cnt * 1.0 / total AS share_of_total, cnt - avg_cnt AS above_average FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Fielding rows are inner-joined to player on player_id, so fielding records with no matching player row are excluded.

NULL and empty-string bats values are each their own group, because GROUP BY keeps them separate. The average count per hand is the mean of the group counts across all groups, including those NULL and blank groups.
Share is the group's count divided by the sum of the group counts. Each player appears in exactly one bats group, so this sum equals the total number of distinct players.
